subject.title: feat(slack): support running as a real Slack user (user identity)

question: Should OpenClaw officially allow an agent to use a human Slack OAuth identity for all enabled reads and writes, and if so what account, scope, attribution, and audit guardrails are required?
rationale: The code can implement the mechanism, but repository policy cannot decide whether broad human-account authority and indistinguishable message attribution are acceptable product and security boundaries.

options.title: Require proof and guardrails
options.body: Keep the feature opt-in but require live DM/group-DM proof, dedicated-account guidance, least-privilege scopes, and explicit attribution and action-authority warnings before merge.

options.title: Accept broad user authority
options.body: Merge the current model after explicitly accepting that enabled Slack actions run with the authorizing human's visibility and identity.

options.title: Keep bot-only core support
options.body: Decline human-identity operation and retain Slack bot identity as the only supported bundled mode.

recommendation.title: Require proof and guardrails
recommendation.body: Keep the feature opt-in but require live DM/group-DM proof, dedicated-account guidance, least-privilege scopes, and explicit attribution and action-authority warnings before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across Slack provider startup, Socket Mode diagnostics, and gateway channel behavior, in addition to proposing this direction.
